verdict.rationale: Greptile's security page says customers can turn off logging to make chats private, and the self-hosted deployment (Docker Compose/Kubernetes, air-gapped) keeps logs on customer servers only. This is real first-party control over what gets retained. However, the same page reserves the right to aggregate and anonymize customer data for analytics and AI training, and no deletion workflow or configurable retention period is documented. Missing for 10: documented data deletion/purge controls, configurable retention windows for the hosted service, an opt-out from de-identified data use for AI training, and independent corroboration.
